headline: The ur-dungeon takes its dice in its pocket
lede: Batch 14 ports ROGUE (1980) to the seed-param contract — and the audit turned up a subtler bug than the one on the ticket: a seeded engine that shares one global dice stream across worlds replays differently the moment two runs step side by side.

notes.text: Rogue's whole game — dungeons, d20 combat, monster AI, hunger, the potion-colour cipher — now lives in a pure sim.js with zero Math.random and zero Date.now, replayable byte-for-byte from ?seed=N at https://www.jalfern.com/retrogames/rogue.

The fix that matters: the RNG position travels INSIDE the game state (randState), so parallel worlds provably cannot interleave entropy. roguecheck proves identical replays while junk worlds step between the actions — a failure mode a module-global stream hides from every one-world-at-a-time test.
Pin floor 44→45. roguecheck joins the fleet: 48 checks, and the mutant proof (flip one stair-check char) collapses winnability 20/20→0/20 before restoring green. feedbackcheck 223/223, build green.

Also shipped around the forge: QA closed the Space Invaders headline gap — destructible bunkers, one brick per shot (#1501) — and Rogue's own polish pass is queued as #1502 (fake doors, missing Amulet win, silent combat).
